title: Microchip Switchtec 160-Lane PCIe Gen6 Switch Shown at FMS 2026 with XpressConnect PCIe 6 Retimer
gist: At FMS 2026 Microchip showed a 160-lane Switchtec PFX 160xG6 PCIe Gen6 switch and a working XpressConnect PCIe Gen6/CXL 3.1 retimer, mounting a credible challenge to Broadcom's decade-long PCIe switch dominance and to Astera Labs, Marvell and Phison in retimers. The structural driver is that PCIe switches and retimers have moved from storage-server plumbing to critical AI infrastructure components, with Gen6's shorter signaling reach in ever-larger systems making retiming a hot market.

insights.claim: Broadcom has been the dominant PCIe switch vendor since its Avago-PLX acquisition more than a decade ago, making PCIe switching an incumbent-heavy market that new Gen6 entrants must displace.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Any share Microchip, Astera Labs or Marvell take in Gen6 switching comes directly out of a Broadcom franchise that has faced little competition for ten years.
insights.quote: Realistically, Broadcom has been the big player in the PCIe switch space since the Avago-PLX acquisition over a decade ago.
insights.locator: Microchip Switchtec PFX 160xG6 Switch Shown at FMS 2026

insights.claim: Microchip's Switchtec PFX 160xG6 is a 160-lane PCIe Gen6 switch chip explicitly positioned to compete with Broadcom, Astera Labs and Marvell, and was shown working on a test PCB at FMS 2026.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Silicon on a test board at a trade show means Microchip is at the sampling/demo stage of Gen6 switching, a checkpoint to track before design wins show up in revenue.
insights.quote: This is a new generation of PCIe switch chip designed to compete with offerings from Broadcom, Astera Labs, and Marvell.
insights.locator: Microchip Switchtec PFX 160xG6 Switch Shown at FMS 2026

insights.claim: PCIe switches have shifted from being tools used mostly in storage servers and fringe deep learning boxes to critical components in modern AI infrastructure build-outs, which is why the segment is heating up.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: PCIe switch TAM is now levered to AI cluster capex rather than to storage-server refresh cycles, changing the growth profile of Broadcom, Astera Labs, Marvell and Microchip connectivity lines.
insights.quote: PCIe switches went from tools mostly in storage servers and the fringe deep learning servers of yesteryear to critical components in modern AI infrastructure build-outs
insights.locator: The space has been heating up as PCIe switches

insights.claim: Microchip appears to be concentrating its Gen6 effort on PCIe rather than CXL switching, diverging from other vendors that are pursuing both PCIe and CXL switches in this generation.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: If CXL switching becomes the higher-value socket in memory-pooled AI systems, Microchip's PCIe-only focus is a strategic gap; if CXL switching stalls, it is a capital-efficient bet.
insights.quote: while other vendors are focusing on PCIe and CXL switches in the Gen6 generation, Microchip seems to be focusing more on PCIe
insights.locator: Notably, while other vendors are focusing

insights.claim: The PFX 160xG6 supports up to 20 ports but real deployments use far fewer because ports are consumed by x16 GPU and NIC attachments, so lane count rather than port count is the binding design constraint in AI servers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Judge competing switch silicon on total lanes and per-lane cost for x16 GPU/NIC fan-out, not on headline port counts.
insights.quote: These switches can have up to 20 ports but usually use far fewer because they are often connected to x16 GPUs and NICs these days.
insights.locator: These switches can have up to 20 ports

insights.claim: Microchip runs a second PCIe switch line, the PSX, described as a more programmable product aimed at storage platforms, separate from the PFX switching family.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Microchip is segmenting AI fan-out switching from programmable storage switching, so its connectivity revenue is not a single AI-linked line.
insights.quote: The company also has a PSX line, which, from what I understand, is more of a programmable line used for a storage platform.

insights.claim: PCIe Gen6 signaling has shorter electrical reach while systems keep growing physically due to component count and cooling requirements, and that mismatch is what makes retimers a hot area of the industry.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Retimer attach rate should rise with every PCIe generation and with liquid-cooled, physically larger AI racks, a compounding volume driver for Astera Labs, Microchip, Broadcom, Marvell and Phison.
insights.quote: PCIe Gen6 signaling generally has shorter reach, and yet systems are growing in size due to the sheer number of components and the cooling they require.
insights.locator: Retimers are important in today’s architectures

insights.claim: NVIDIA has been trying to design its systems around the use of retimers, a direct headwind to retimer content per AI server even as reach limits push the other way.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Retimer suppliers face platform risk from the largest AI system designer engineering the part out; watch NVIDIA reference designs for retimer content as a leading indicator for Astera Labs and peers.
insights.quote: Retimers are important in today’s architectures even as NVIDIA has been trying to design around their use.
insights.locator: Microchip XpressConnect PCIe Gen6 Retimer Shown

insights.claim: Microchip's XpressConnect retimer was demonstrated live retiming a PCIe Gen6 link on the FMS 2026 show floor, and it can also retime CXL 3.1.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Dual PCIe Gen6 and CXL 3.1 retiming makes the part addressable to both GPU fan-out and memory-pooling designs, doubling its socket opportunity.
insights.quote: Microchip’s XpressConnect can also retime CXL 3.1.

insights.claim: The CXL retimer market has taken off and Astera Labs' Aries 6 already handles CXL, so CXL capability is becoming table stakes rather than a differentiator in Gen6 retimers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Feature parity on CXL points to price and supply competition ahead in retimers, a margin risk for the incumbent leader Astera Labs.
insights.quote: That is important since this market has taken off and competition like the Astera Labs Aries 6 can do CXL as well.

insights.claim: Broadcom, Marvell and Phison are all working on retimer solutions alongside Microchip and Astera Labs, making retimers a crowded five-plus-vendor space rather than a duopoly.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Crowding argues against durable pricing power in retimers even with strong unit growth; prefer exposure via volume and attach rate rather than assumed margin expansion.
insights.quote: It is an interesting and competitive space with companies Broadcom, Marvell, and Phison all working on solutions.

insights.claim: Everpure announced in the week before August 13, 2026 that a second top-5 hyperscaler will use its DirectFlash technology, following Meta as the first hyperscaler adopter per ServeTheHome's understanding.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A second top-5 hyperscaler validates DirectFlash as more than a single-customer design win and signals hyperscaler willingness to displace conventional SSD form factors at scale.
insights.quote: this week, Everpure announced that a second top 5 hyper-scaler will be using its DirectFlash technology in a big win for the company. The first hyper-scaler using it is Meta, from what we understand.
insights.locator: Bonus: Everpure DirectFlash Module on Display

insights.claim: An Everpure DirectFlash module appearing on display in Microchip's own FMS booth suggests Microchip silicon is inside the module, a supplier relationship normally hidden because such modules are usually shown as opaque models.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: If Microchip supplies the controller silicon inside DirectFlash modules, hyperscaler DirectFlash adoption becomes an indirect volume driver for Microchip storage controllers.
insights.quote: Usually we see models like this, so we do not get to see who is running inside the module, but being in the Microchip booth, we have some idea.
insights.locator: Bonus: Everpure DirectFlash Module on Display
